newsitem.title: NORWAY: BP finds gas in Norway's deepwater Nyk area.
newsitem.headline: BP finds gas in Norway's deepwater Nyk area.

text.p: The Norwegian Oil Directorate (OD) said on Thursday that British Petroleum Norge had found gas from deepwater exploration drilling in the frontier Nyk High area in the Norwegian Sea.

The OD said it was too early to give precise figures for the size of the find, but preliminary estimates indicated between 40 to 60 million cubic metres of oil equivalent gas, or almost half the size of the North Sea Frigg field.
"The probability of finding more gas in the area is extremely high, but there also are many indications that oil will be found," the OD said in a statement.

BP was awarded operatorship of licence 218 in Norway's 15th licensing round last year and holds a 25 percent stake. It is partnered by state oil company Den norske stats oljeselskap AS and Saga Petroleum ASA with 10 percent.
The OD said well 6707/10-1 was drilled to a depth of 3,900 meters below sea level in a water depth of 1,274 metres. It is the first deepwater well to be spudded on the Norwegian continental shelf.
It said that the gas primarily contained methane, but traces of heavier hydrocarbons were also registered. It added that water and not oil had been found under the gas column.
Drilling is due to continue for another 1,000 metres.
